Template scaffolded: `report-template.html` (11.5 KB, fully offline, no JS). Here's the structure and why:

## Document Outline

```
html lang="en"
├── head
│   ├── meta charset / viewport / title
│   └── <style>  ← all CSS inline, incl. @media print
└── body
    ├── header      → h1 + report metadata (dl.meta)
    ├── nav         → optional linked TOC (delete if unwanted)
    ├── main
    │   ├── section#summary      → Executive Summary
    │   ├── section#dashboard    → RAG tiles
    │   ├── section#milestones   → milestone table
    │   ├── section#progress     → accomplishments list
    │   ├── section#upcoming     → next-period commitments
    │   ├── section#risks        → risk/issue register table
    │   ├── section#decisions    → sponsor asks table
    │   ├── section#budget       → spend vs. plan table
    │   ├── section#changes      → change-request log
    │   └── section#appendix     → glossary + references
    └── footer      → confidentiality + contact
```

## Element Choices (semantic, not decorative)

| Content | Element | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Report metadata | `<dl>` | Label/value pairs are literally what a definition list is |
| RAG ratings | `<data class="rag rag-red" value="red">` | Visible text + machine-readable value for future scraping |
| Dates | `<time datetime="2026-10-15">` | Sortable, parseable, locale-independent |
| % complete | `<meter min="0" max="100">` | Native visual gauge; falls back to readable text |
| All tabular data | `<table>` + `<caption>` + `th scope="col"` | Correct semantics, accessible, and tables are what non-technical editors find easiest to edit |
| Glossary | `<dl>` again | Same reasoning as metadata |
| Sections | `<section>` + `<h2>`, exactly one `<h1>` | Clean heading outline that screen readers and TOC generators can traverse |

## Editability Conventions

- **`[BRACKETED TOKENS]`** mark every fill point, highlighted with a `.placeholder` style (yellow halo) that auto-disappears in print
- `<!-- EDIT: ... -->` comments state the fill rule at each spot (e.g., "3–5 sentences, verdict first")
- Flat nesting — content sits in plain text nodes, no deep wrapper soup; anyone can edit in any text editor
- Modular sections: budget/changes/TOC can be deleted whole without breaking layout
- RAG coloring is a one-class swap (`rag-green` → `rag-red`), no CSS knowledge needed

## Print/A11y built in

- `@media print` with `break-inside: avoid` on rows/tiles and `break-after: avoid` on headings — browser Print-to-PDF yields a clean A4/Letter document
- `scope="col"` headers, captions on every table, single `<h1>` — screen-reader friendly out of the box
